newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - France - Le Monde June 26.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.
-- French government sources confirm partial privatisation of France Telecom in the autumn being considered.
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn not opposed to partial France Telecom privatisation. Prime Minister Lionel Jospin has not yet studied issue directly.
-- Employment Minister Martine Aubry critical of plans by French carmaker Peugeot to shed 2,816 jobs in 1997.
-- Chemicals and drugs group Rhone-Poulenc to buy all outstanding shares in U.S. unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, regroup its chemical, fibre and polymer operations in one unit and list it on Paris bourse.

-- French computer services company Cap Gemini chief executive sees 1997 net profit of more than 500 million francs and profit of 700-800 million in 1998. Says firm free to make acquisitions following Daimler-Benz decision to sell its 24.4 percent stake in Gemini.
-- French stock market at record high. Reassured that new government appears to be watering down some its campaign promises, boosted by influx of capital from foreign investors.
